summary: Iteration 40 — full backend + frontend coverage for the PearBlue Mailbox fuzzy-match + external-auto-ticket feature. BACKEND (pytest 18/18 pass, test_iteration40.py): (a) _classify_notification returns correct (kind,name,collection) for all 4 subject patterns; priority order verified (review beats generic contact fallback); ambiguous → generic contact; empty/no-match → (None,None,None). (b) _is_own_notification_sender: resend.dev, notifications.resend.com, pearblue.nl → True; external customer domain → False; quota/delivery-failed subjects always treated as own. (c) POST /api/admin/mailboxes/rebuild-matches: requires auth (401/403 without token), returns {checked,matched,auto_created} with correct types, matched<=checked, and second call is bounded (r2.matched <= r1.matched). (d) GET /api/admin/mailboxes/ingested returns list with matched_kind values in the allowed set {contact,review,registration,chat_handoff,contact_auto}; DB inspection confirmed 97/145 have matched_kind and 37 have ticket_ref (all 37 are auto_created contact_auto rows). FRONTEND (Playwright): /admin → Mailboxen (IMAP) tab renders cms-mailboxes; 100 mailbox-ingest-row-{i} items shown; 57 emerald mailbox-ingest-matched-{i} chips with correct text like '✓ contact · Tester' and title='contact · Tester'; 8 pear #TKT-XXXXXX chips (mailbox-ingest-tkt-*); 35 amber 'Zonder ticket' pills. mailbox-rebuild-matches button visible with correct label '🔄 Match bestaande opnieuw'. Click → POST /admin/mailboxes/rebuild-matches → 200 {checked:108, matched:60, auto_created:0}; toast 'Opnieuw gematcht: 60 van 108' shown; list reloaded (no page refresh).
critical_code_review_comments: rebuild-matches: `matched` counter is NOT fully idempotent for kinds review/registration/contact where the source doc has no ticket_ref. Those rows never get a ticket_ref set on the ingest row, so they still satisfy the query filter {ticket_ref: null} on every subsequent call and are re-matched each time (matched counter increments). Consider filtering rows where {matched_kind: null} instead of ticket_ref null, so already-matched-but-no-ticket rows are skipped. Right now the endpoint reports 'matched: 60' every run even though nothing changed in the DB — misleading UX in the toast ('60 opnieuw gematcht' after nothing happened).

The generic contact fallback regex `\[PearBlue\]\s+.+?\s+[—-]+\s+(.+?)\s*$` is broad and will match ANY [PearBlue]-prefixed subject with an em-dash — including future notification types that haven't been added yet, misclassifying them as 'contact'. Consider adding a warning log when the generic fallback fires so new types are detected.

_create_ticket_from_email inserts a contact_message with `source: 'imap_auto'` and `priority: 'P3'` — but no dedup on subject/from_email hash across multiple UIDs. If the same customer sends 3 emails with slightly different Message-IDs, 3 separate tickets are created. Consider grouping by (from_email, normalized_subject) within a 24h window.

OWN_NOTIFICATION_DOMAINS is a hard-coded set. If a customer legitimately emails from a resend.dev alias (rare but possible for testing), their mail will silently be skipped by auto-ticket creation. Consider making this configurable via env (e.g., IMAP_OWN_DOMAINS='resend.dev,pearblue.nl,...').

The endpoint runs a `find({$or:[{ticket_ref:None},{ticket_ref:{$exists:False}}]})` without any pagination or limit. For a mailbox with tens of thousands of unmatched rows, this could time out (default 60s HTTP). Add a batch limit (e.g., process 500/call) and return `has_more:true` so UI can loop, or run it in a background task.
